question: In the full playthrough, who were the first boss (the character whose long health bar appears at the bottom of the screen) and the last boss that the player defeated using the weapon 'Beast Staff: Golden Eyes' (after which that weapon was no longer used)?
reference_answer: Fire Spirit Primordial Mother, Great Shigandang (大石敢当)

db_evidence.notes: The weapon-forging event ('降妖·金睛', attack 105) at 74490s is clearly and reliably retrievable via topic_facts/episodes (contains the literal string 金睛). The two boss fights at the clue intervals are present in visual_clips/topic_facts as generic visual descriptions (e.g. 'tall gaunt boss with red glowing patterns and long pale hair' for [74716,74795]; a fight with on-screen text '慈悲' and a 'glowing blue nodules' creature for the fight nearest [80807,80881]), but in no table (entities, topic_facts, event_steps, semantic_triples, object_states) is the boss's actual name/identity text captured for either clue interval -- the underlying 30-sec captioner never OCR'd or named the Chinese boss-name UI text for these fights, and in fact repeatedly mislabels the game itself as Elden Ring / Nioh 2 / Dark Souls 3 / Sekiro instead of Black Myth: Wukong in the surrounding captions, indicating the captioning backbone struggles with this game's HUD/visual style. This forces every rollout to rely entirely on clip_qa (the visual sub-agent) to read boss names from raw frames, and none of the 5 rollouts' clip_qa windows exactly covered the true last-boss clue interval [80807,80881] (closest attempt: 80400-80640, rollout 2).

root_causes: Boss identity text is not captured anywhere in the pre-built memory DB for either clue interval -- captions describe boss appearance generically but never extract/OCR the on-screen Chinese boss name, so SQL/semantic search over any table cannot recover the reference names and every rollout must fall back to clip_qa guesses.

The visual sub-agent (clip_qa) produced a different boss name in nearly every rollout for what is likely the same first-boss fight (Flint Vanguard x3, Great Sage's Broken Shell x1, Shigandang x1), none matching the reference 'Fire Spirit Primordial Mother' -- indicating unreliable/hallucinated reading of small on-screen name text rather than a consistent misread.

All 5 rollouts undershot the true last-boss clue window [80807,80881] by 150-5000+ seconds when deciding where the golden-eyes staff was last used, most commonly stopping their search around 75960-80640s at the first clearly-identifiable late-game boss fight rather than continuing to scan all the way to 80807s.

Two rollouts (0, 1) treated an early, nearby fight (~75960s) as the definitive 'last use' of the weapon and never searched further in time at all, compounding the last-boss error with an extremely large temporal miss.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly located the weapon-forging event ('降妖·金睛' / Beast Staff: Golden Eyes, attack 105) at 74490s via run_sql/semantic_search on episodes and topic_facts, establishing a correct start-of-usage anchor.

Rollout 3's clip_qa windows (74680-75100, 74690-74810) correctly covered the true first-boss clue interval [74716,74795], showing the retrieval/time-window strategy can hit the right interval when the agent searches broadly enough around the weapon-forge anchor.
Rollout 2's last-boss clip_qa window (80400-80640) came within ~170s of the true clue interval [80807,80881], the closest any rollout got.
transferable_lessons: When a question hinges on an in-game HUD name/label (boss name, item name) that this DB's captioner does not reliably OCR, do not trust a single clip_qa read of a narrow window -- issue clip_qa over multiple overlapping windows and cross-check the returned name against entities/topic_facts for corroboration before submitting, since the visual sub-agent can hallucinate plausible-but-wrong boss names.

For 'last time X happened' questions, do not stop the search at the first later candidate event found near a coarse hour-level summary -- explicitly scan run_sql/topic_facts across the full remaining span of interest (here, all boss fights between 74490s and the point of the next weapon change) before declaring a 'last' occurrence.

When an hour-level or multi-hour episode summary lists several boss names in sequence, use it only to generate a shortlist of candidate windows to clip_qa-verify individually -- treating the summary's last-mentioned boss as ground truth (as several rollouts implicitly did) skips the true final fight that occurs later in the raw captions.

If early captions for a video segment show signs of engine/game misidentification (e.g. this DB repeatedly calling Black Myth: Wukong 'Elden Ring' or 'Nioh 2'), treat entity/name extraction in that segment as low-confidence and prioritize direct clip_qa frame reads over trusting extracted text fields.
